Growable worklists
=================

Import Worklists.module's Growable theory and write:

  (worklist-push int size_t realloc buffer length capacity value)

element and count are declaration specifiers. count must be an unsigned
integral type admitted by the native overflow builtins. The allocator has
the exact signature void *(void *, count). buffer is a modifiable element*
object; length and capacity are distinct modifiable count objects. The
supplied value has the element type.

The five executable arguments are acquired in this order: allocator,
buffer address, length address, capacity address, value. Each is evaluated
once, including on failure. The callback is invoked only when growth is
required, and at most once per push.

The macro returns int 1 on success and 0 on failure. Capacity begins at 8
elements and doubles on growth. Both doubling and capacity*sizeof(element)
are checked before allocation. A failed allocation, size overflow, aliased
length/capacity, excessive length, or null buffer with nonzero capacity
leaves the buffer pointer, length, capacity and existing elements unchanged.
On success the old prefix is retained, value is appended, and length grows
by one. The allocator must have realloc-like ownership: NULL preserves the
old allocation, and success returns a block retaining the old contents.

The caller supplies valid objects and an owned allocation whose actual extent
matches capacity. The buffer pointer object and counters must not overlap.
The macro does not introduce return, break, continue or goto. Callers can pop
in LIFO order using buffer[--length], or inspect the retained prefix directly.

The allocator and all state are explicit arguments. No caller-local queue,
environment, failure label or capacity name is captured by the library.
Ordinary C headers and native callback functions remain compiler inputs.

The native test fixture adapts the growable stack pattern used by constructor
scanners and deep-copy worklists. It does not change downstream runtime code.
